001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
004import java.net.URI;
005import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
006import java.nio.CharBuffer;
007import java.nio.charset.CharacterCodingException;
008import java.nio.charset.Charset;
009import java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder;
010import java.nio.charset.CodingErrorAction;
011import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
012
013import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder.Buffer.DirectByteBufferBuffer;
014import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder.Buffer.StringBuilderBuffer;
015import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.ContentType;
016import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.ContentType.StandardContentType;
017import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.WriteMethod;
018import io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.AbstractStandardEventFormatter;
019
020/**
021 * Encodes a {@link LogEvent} into a buffer of its choosing. While the {@link Buffer} does
022 * not need to be thread-safe the encoder itself should be.
023 * <p>
024 * An appender typically calls an encoder by first {@linkplain #buffer(BufferHints)
025 * creating a buffer} that the encoder knows about or reusing an existing {@link Buffer}
026 * the encoder knows about.
027 * <p>
028 * The {@linkplain #encode(LogEvent, Buffer) encoding into a buffer} typically happens
029 * outside of lock to minimize lock contention. Thus the appender promises not to share a
030 * buffer at the same time with other threads as well as only use a buffer the log encoder
031 * created at some point.
032 * <p>
033 * Once encoding is done the appender than typically enters into a lock (appenders
034 * attached to an async publisher may not need to use a lock) where the appender will ask
035 * the buffer to {@linkplain Buffer#drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) drain} its contents into
036 * the output.
037 * <p>
038 * Because {@link Buffer} is not a specific implementation the Encoder typically casts the
039 * buffer to the expected concrete implementation. {@link AbstractEncoder} can make this
040 * logic easier and is recommended to extend it.
041 * <p>
042 * Given the complexity of encoders it is recommend use the much easier to implement
043 * interface of {@link LogFormatter} and convert it to an encoder with
044 * {@link #of(LogFormatter)}.
045 *
046 * @see LogFormatter
047 * @see Buffer
048 * @see LogAppender
049 * @see StringBuilderBuffer
050 */
051public interface LogEncoder {
052
053        /**
054         * Creates a <strong>new</strong> buffer. The encoder should not try to reuse buffers
055         * as that is the responsibility of the {@linkplain LogAppender appender} (and
056         * possibly {@link LogOutput} but usually not). Hints can be retrieved by call
057         * {@link LogOutput#bufferHints()}.
058         * @param hints hints are like size and storage type etc.
059         * @return a new buffer.
060         * @apiNote hints can be retrieved by calling {@link LogOutput#bufferHints()} the
061         * reason the output itself is not passed is to prevent the buffer from using the
062         * output directly at an inappropriate time as well as the rare possibility of the
063         * buffer being used by multiple outputs.
064         */
065        public Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints);
066
067        /**
068         * Encodes an event to the buffer. It is recommended that the encoder call
069         * {@link Buffer#clear()} before using.
070         * @param event log event.
071         * @param buffer buffer created from {@link #buffer(BufferHints)}.
072         */
073        public void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer);
074
075        /**
076         * Creates an encoder from a formatter that encodes with
077         * {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}.
078         * @param formatter formatter.
079         * @return encoder.
080         */
081        public static LogEncoder of(LogFormatter formatter) {
082                return of(formatter, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
083        }
084
085        /**
086         * Creates an encoder from a formatter that encodes with the given charset and reports
087         * {@link StandardContentType#TEXT_PLAIN} with that charset to the output.
088         * @param formatter formatter.
089         * @param charset charset to encode with. Only affects outputs whose
090         * {@link BufferHints#writeMethod()} is {@link WriteMethod#BYTES} or
091         * {@link WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER} - the {@link WriteMethod#STRING} path hands a plain
092         * {@link String} to {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, String)}, whose own default
093         * implementation is fixed to {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8} regardless of this
094         * parameter, but no built-in output actually uses that write method.
095         * @return encoder.
096         */
097        public static LogEncoder of(LogFormatter formatter, Charset charset) {
098                return of(formatter, charset, ContentType.of(StandardContentType.TEXT_PLAIN.contentType(), charset));
099        }
100
101        /**
102         * Creates an encoder from a formatter that reports the given content type to the
103         * output, encoding with {@link ContentType#charsetOrNull() its charset} if specified,
104         * otherwise {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}. Use this instead of
105         * {@link #of(LogFormatter, Charset)} when the formatter produces something other than
106         * plain text (e.g. a custom {@link ContentType.DefaultContentType}).
107         * @param formatter formatter.
108         * @param contentType content type reported to the output. See
109         * {@link #of(LogFormatter, Charset)} for the effect of its charset.
110         * @return encoder.
111         */
112        public static LogEncoder of(LogFormatter formatter, ContentType contentType) {
113                var charset = contentType.charsetOrNull();
114                return of(formatter, charset == null ? StandardCharsets.UTF_8 : charset, contentType);
115        }
116
117        private static LogEncoder of(LogFormatter formatter, Charset charset, ContentType contentType) {
118                return new FormatterEncoder(formatter, charset, contentType);
119        }
120
121        /**
122         * Provides a lazy loaded encoder from a URI.
123         * @param uri uri.
124         * @return provider of encoder.
125         */
126        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> of(URI uri) {
127                return of(LogProviderRef.of(uri));
128        }
129
130        /**
131         * Provides the standard TTLL encoder.
132         * @return provider of encoder.
133         */
134        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> ofTTLL() {
135                return of(LogProviderRef.of(URI.create(AbstractStandardEventFormatter.SCHEMA)));
136        }
137
138        /**
139         * Provides a lazy loaded encoder from a provider ref.
140         * @param ref uri.
141         * @return provider of output.
142         * @apiNote the provider may throw an {@link UncheckedIOException}.
143         */
144        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> of(LogProviderRef ref) {
145                return (s, c) -> {
146                        return c.encoderRegistry().provide(ref).provide(s, c);
147                };
148        }
149
150        /**
151         * Finds output based on URI.
152         */
153        public interface EncoderProvider {
154
155                /**
156                 * Loads an encoder from a URI.
157                 * @param ref reference to provider usually just a uri.
158                 * @return output.
159                 * @throws LogProviderRef.NotFoundException if there is no registered provider.
160                 */
161                LogProvider<LogEncoder> provide(LogProviderRef ref) throws LogProviderRef.NotFoundException;
162
163                /**
164                 * Convenience method to register encoders that require no configuration.
165                 * @param encoder already configured encoder.
166                 * @return encoder provider.
167                 */
168                static EncoderProvider of(LogEncoder encoder) {
169                        return ref -> LogProvider.of(encoder);
170                }
171
172        }
173
174        /**
175         * Encoders buffer.
176         */
177        public interface Buffer extends AutoCloseable {
178
179                /**
180                 * The appender will call this usually within a lock to transfer content from the
181                 * buffer to the output.
182                 * @param output output to receive content.
183                 * @param event log event.
184                 */
185                public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event);
186
187                /**
188                 * Prepare the buffer for reuse.
189                 * <p>
190                 * An appender may not call clear before being passed to the encoder so the
191                 * encoder should do its own clearing.
192                 */
193                public void clear();
194
195                /**
196                 * Convenience that will call clear.
197                 */
198                @Override
199                default void close() {
200                        clear();
201                }
202
203                /**
204                 * A buffer that simply wraps a {@link StringBuilder}. Direct access to the
205                 * {@link StringBuilder} is available as the field {@link #stringBuilder}.
206                 *
207                 * @see AbstractEncoder
208                 */
209                public final class StringBuilderBuffer implements Buffer {
210
211                        /**
212                         * Underlying StringBuilder.
213                         */
214                        public final StringBuilder stringBuilder;
215
216                        /**
217                         * Creates a StringBuilder based buffer.
218                         * @param sb string builder.
219                         * @return buffer.
220                         */
221                        public static StringBuilderBuffer of(StringBuilder sb) {
222                                return new StringBuilderBuffer(sb);
223                        }
224
225                        private StringBuilderBuffer(StringBuilder stringBuilder) {
226                                super();
227                                this.stringBuilder = stringBuilder;
228                        }
229
230                        @Override
231                        public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event) {
232                                output.write(event, stringBuilder.toString());
233                        }
234
235                        @Override
236                        public void clear() {
237                                stringBuilder.setLength(0);
238                        }
239
240                }
241
242                /**
243                 * A buffer that formats into a reused {@link StringBuilder} (like
244                 * {@link StringBuilderBuffer}) but encodes directly into a reused
245                 * {@link ByteBuffer} via a {@link CharsetEncoder}, instead of going through an
246                 * intermediate {@code String} and {@code byte[]} the way
247                 * {@code LogOutput.write(LogEvent, String)}'s default implementation does. This
248                 * is the same technique
249                 * <a href="https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/manual/garbagefree.html">Log4j2's
250                 * garbage-free logging</a> uses.
251                 * <p>
252                 * The {@link CharsetEncoder} work happens in {@link #encodeToByteBuffer()},
253                 * called by the encoder's {@code encode(LogEvent, Buffer)} step - i.e. before
254                 * {@link #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) drain}, which appenders that separate
255                 * formatting from writing ({@code LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender},
256                 * {@code SynchronizedThreadLocalBufferLogAppender}) call outside their lock.
257                 * {@code drain} - called from inside the lock - therefore does nothing but write
258                 * the already-encoded bytes, matching how Log4j2 confines the actual
259                 * character-to-byte transcoding to a thread-local scratch buffer and synchronizes
260                 * only the final copy into the shared destination.
261                 * <p>
262                 * Constructed for a specific {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod} - either
263                 * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}, in which case {@link #drain} calls
264                 * {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, LogOutput.ContentType)} directly,
265                 * or {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTES}, in which case {@link #drain} calls
266                 * {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, byte[], int, int, LogOutput.ContentType)}
267                 * using the backing array directly, rather than going through
268                 * {@code LogOutput#write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, ContentType)}'s default
269                 * implementation (which would allocate a fresh {@code byte[]} copy every call for
270                 * an output that does not itself implement that overload).
271                 * <p>
272                 * Not thread-safe. Like all {@link Buffer}s it relies on the appender to
273                 * guarantee no overlapping use.
274                 */
275                public final class DirectByteBufferBuffer implements Buffer {
276
277                        /**
278                         * Default initial byte buffer capacity, matching Log4j2's own
279                         * {@code log4j2.encoderByteBufferSize} default.
280                         */
281                        public static final int DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY = 8192;
282
283                        /**
284                         * The buffer the formatter writes characters into.
285                         */
286                        public final StringBuilder stringBuilder = new StringBuilder();
287
288                        private final CharsetEncoder charsetEncoder;
289
290                        private final LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod;
291
292                        private final LogOutput.ContentType contentType;
293
294                        private ByteBuffer byteBuffer;
295
296                        /**
297                         * Creates a buffer with the default initial byte capacity and
298                         * {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}.
299                         * @param writeMethod which {@link LogOutput#write} overload {@link #drain}
300                         * should call - {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTES} or
301                         * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}.
302                         */
303                        public DirectByteBufferBuffer(LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod) {
304                                this(writeMethod, DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
305                        }
306
307                        /**
308                         * Creates a buffer with the given write method, initial byte capacity and
309                         * charset.
310                         * @param writeMethod which {@link LogOutput#write} overload {@link #drain}
311                         * should call - {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTES} or
312                         * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}.
313                         * @param initialByteCapacity initial capacity of the byte buffer. It will
314                         * grow (doubling, or to whatever a single event needs if larger) as needed
315                         * and the grown capacity is kept for subsequent events.
316                         * @param charset charset to encode with.
317                         */
318                        public DirectByteBufferBuffer(LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod, int initialByteCapacity, Charset charset) {
319                                this(writeMethod, initialByteCapacity, charset,
320                                                LogOutput.ContentType.of(StandardContentType.TEXT_PLAIN.contentType(), charset));
321                        }
322
323                        /**
324                         * Creates a buffer with the given write method, initial byte capacity,
325                         * charset and content type to report to the output.
326                         * @param writeMethod which {@link LogOutput#write} overload {@link #drain}
327                         * should call - {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTES} or
328                         * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}.
329                         * @param initialByteCapacity initial capacity of the byte buffer. It will
330                         * grow (doubling, or to whatever a single event needs if larger) as needed
331                         * and the grown capacity is kept for subsequent events.
332                         * @param charset charset to encode with.
333                         * @param contentType content type reported to {@link LogOutput#write}. Its
334                         * {@link LogOutput.ContentType#charsetOrNull() charset}, if specified, should
335                         * normally match {@code charset}.
336                         */
337                        public DirectByteBufferBuffer(LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod, int initialByteCapacity, Charset charset,
338                                        LogOutput.ContentType contentType) {
339                                this.writeMethod = writeMethod;
340                                this.byteBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(initialByteCapacity);
341                                this.charsetEncoder = charset.newEncoder()
342                                        .onMalformedInput(CodingErrorAction.REPLACE)
343                                        .onUnmappableCharacter(CodingErrorAction.REPLACE);
344                                this.contentType = contentType;
345                        }
346
347                        /**
348                         * Writes the already-encoded bytes to the output. Assumes
349                         * {@link #encodeToByteBuffer()} has already been called for this event - see
350                         * the class doc for why that step lives in the encoder instead of here.
351                         */
352                        @Override
353                        public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event) {
354                                switch (writeMethod) {
355                                        case BYTE_BUFFER -> output.write(event, byteBuffer, contentType);
356                                        case BYTES -> output.write(event, byteBuffer.array(),
357                                                        byteBuffer.arrayOffset() + byteBuffer.position(), byteBuffer.remaining(), contentType);
358                                        case STRING ->
359                                                throw new IllegalStateException("DirectByteBufferBuffer does not support WriteMethod.STRING");
360                                }
361                        }
362
363                        /**
364                         * Encodes the current contents of {@link #stringBuilder} into the reused
365                         * {@link ByteBuffer}, growing it first if needed. Deliberately not called
366                         * from {@link #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent)} - see the class doc.
367                         */
368                        void encodeToByteBuffer() {
369                                int maxBytes = (int) Math.ceil(stringBuilder.length() * (double) charsetEncoder.maxBytesPerChar());
370                                if (byteBuffer.capacity() < maxBytes) {
371                                        byteBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(Math.max(maxBytes, byteBuffer.capacity() * 2));
372                                }
373                                byteBuffer.clear();
374                                charsetEncoder.reset();
375                                CharBuffer cb = CharBuffer.wrap(stringBuilder);
376                                var result = charsetEncoder.encode(cb, byteBuffer, true);
377                                if (result.isError()) {
378                                        try {
379                                                result.throwException();
380                                        }
381                                        catch (CharacterCodingException e) {
382                                                throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
383                                        }
384                                }
385                                /*
386                                 * maxBytes above already sized the buffer to fit the worst case so flush
387                                 * should never overflow, but check defensively rather than silently
388                                 * truncate.
389                                 */
390                                var flushResult = charsetEncoder.flush(byteBuffer);
391                                if (flushResult.isOverflow()) {
392                                        throw new IllegalStateException("CharsetEncoder flush overflowed despite pre-sized buffer");
393                                }
394                                byteBuffer.flip();
395                        }
396
397                        @Override
398                        public void clear() {
399                                stringBuilder.setLength(0);
400                        }
401
402                }
403
404        }
405
406        /**
407         * Hints the output can pass to the encoder for creating buffers like max size and
408         * storage style of the buffer etc.
409         *
410         * @apiNote There is no guarantees the encoder/buffer will honor these hints.
411         */
412        public interface BufferHints {
413
414                /*
415                 * TODO should we seal this?
416                 */
417
418                /**
419                 * The preferred write style of the output.
420                 * @return write method.
421                 * @apiNote {@link WriteMethod} implements this interface for convenience.
422                 */
423                LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod();
424
425                /**
426                 * Maximum size of the buffer. This is a way for the encoder to say it can only
427                 * handle so much data per event.
428                 * @return a negative number indicates size is not important.
429                 */
430                default int maximumSize() {
431                        return -1;
432                }
433
434        }
435
436        /**
437         * Abstract encoder that will cast the buffer to the desired implementation. Extend to
438         * make creating encoders easier.
439         *
440         * @param <T> buffer type.
441         */
442        abstract class AbstractEncoder<T extends Buffer> implements LogEncoder {
443
444                /**
445                 * Do nothing constructor.
446                 */
447                protected AbstractEncoder() {
448
449                }
450
451                /**
452                 * Create a specific buffer implementation.
453                 * @param hints buffer creation hints.
454                 * @return buffer
455                 */
456                protected abstract T doBuffer(BufferHints hints);
457
458                /**
459                 * A type safe version of {@link #encode(LogEvent, Buffer)}.
460                 * @param event event.
461                 * @param buffer casted buffer.
462                 */
463                protected abstract void doEncode(LogEvent event, T buffer);
464
465                @Override
466                public final Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints) {
467                        return doBuffer(hints);
468                }
469
470                @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
471                @Override
472                public final void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer) {
473                        doEncode(event, (T) buffer);
474
475                }
476
477        }
478
479}
480
481/*
482 * Not an AbstractEncoder since it needs to hand out either a StringBuilderBuffer or a
483 * DirectByteBufferBuffer depending on the output's WriteMethod hint - see buffer(hints).
484 */
485final class FormatterEncoder implements LogEncoder {
486
487        private final LogFormatter formatter;
488
489        private final Charset charset;
490
491        private final ContentType contentType;
492
493        public FormatterEncoder(LogFormatter formatter, Charset charset, ContentType contentType) {
494                super();
495                this.formatter = formatter;
496                this.charset = charset;
497                this.contentType = contentType;
498        }
499
500        @Override
501        public Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints) {
502                return switch (hints.writeMethod()) {
503                        case STRING -> StringBuilderBuffer.of(new StringBuilder());
504                        case BYTES, BYTE_BUFFER -> new DirectByteBufferBuffer(hints.writeMethod(),
505                                        DirectByteBufferBuffer.DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY, charset, contentType);
506                };
507        }
508
509        @Override
510        public void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer) {
511                switch (buffer) {
512                        case StringBuilderBuffer sb -> {
513                                sb.clear();
514                                formatter.format(sb.stringBuilder, event);
515                        }
516                        case DirectByteBufferBuffer bb -> {
517                                bb.clear();
518                                formatter.format(bb.stringBuilder, event);
519                                bb.encodeToByteBuffer();
520                        }
521                        default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Unsupported buffer: " + buffer.getClass());
522                }
523        }
524
525}
